lessons.title: Values, names, operators and units
lessons.motivation: Feature units and types determine what a price expression means, before syntax is introduced.
lessons.progression: Change numeric area to text and explain why repetition is not a prediction.
lessons.terms: assignment, int, float, str, bool, expression, operator, precedence.
lessons.math: Variables and function evaluation; numbers carry feature/target units.
lessons.worked: area=2; weight=100; bias=50; prediction=area*weight+bias gives 250 ($k); '2'*3 gives '222', not 6.
lessons.misconception: Assignment is not algebraic equality; a numeric-looking string is not a number.

objectives.outcome: Classify numeric, text and boolean feature values.
objectives.assessment: Choose the type of a new customer record field.
objectives.remediation: Compare a type-tagged value table.

objectives.outcome: Evaluate a weighted expression with correct types, order and units.
objectives.assessment: Predict a changed feature rule and reject string repetition as multiplication.
objectives.remediation: Substitute values into the Algebra weighted-sum trace.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish reassignment from an equality comparison.
objectives.assessment: Predict the final value after two assignments versus ==.
objectives.remediation: Step through the name/value table.

objectives.outcome: Choose parentheses and safe numeric conversion for a supplied expression.
objectives.assessment: Repair a preset precedence or conversion slot.
objectives.remediation: Compare expression trees and conversion failure examples.

lessons.title: Collections, order, indexing and mutation
lessons.motivation: Ordered features and keyed records solve different identification problems; names may share one object.
lessons.progression: Reorder a feature pair and contrast alias versus copy after one edit.
lessons.terms: list, tuple, dict, set, index, slice, key, reference, mutation.
lessons.math: Ordered feature vectors; row identity differs from numeric position.
lessons.worked: features=[2,10]; alias=features; alias[0]=3 changes features to [3,10]. features[-1] is 10; features[:1] is [3].
lessons.misconception: A slice excludes its stop; aliasing is not an independent copy; a set has no feature-column order.

objectives.outcome: Select an appropriate collection for ordered features, fixed pairs, keyed records and unique labels.
objectives.assessment: Match four ML data requirements to collection types.
objectives.remediation: Rebuild a record using named keys and an ordered vector.

objectives.outcome: Preserve feature order and identify shared-reference mutation.
objectives.assessment: Predict both aliases after an edit and explain an independent-copy repair.
objectives.remediation: Draw two names pointing to one list, then copy it.

objectives.outcome: Predict positive/negative indexing and half-open slices.
objectives.assessment: Select the exact resulting values from a changed sequence.
objectives.remediation: Mark start-inclusive/stop-exclusive positions.

objectives.outcome: Use dictionary keys and set membership without relying on set iteration order.
objectives.assessment: Repair a preset keyed lookup or membership check.
objectives.remediation: Contrast position, key and membership tables.

lessons.title: Conditions and explicit missing-value rules
lessons.motivation: A validation rule decides which observations the model is allowed to see.
lessons.progression: Contrast valid age zero, missing age and a boundary threshold.
lessons.math: Domains, Boolean predicates and threshold decisions.
lessons.worked: age=0 is valid but age=None is missing. if age is None: flag_missing=True must not be replaced by if not age.
lessons.misconception: Zero, False and missing do not mean the same thing; = is not ==.

objectives.outcome: Evaluate comparisons and compound Boolean conditions.
objectives.assessment: Predict a new bounded eligibility/validation predicate.
objectives.remediation: Build its truth table one condition at a time.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish a legitimate zero from None in a data rule.
objectives.assessment: Repair a missingness branch and justify why zero is retained.
objectives.remediation: Compare records with 0, None and an ordinary positive value.

objectives.outcome: Trace mutually exclusive if/elif/else branches.
objectives.assessment: Choose which output is reached at boundary values.
objectives.remediation: Annotate the first satisfied branch.

objectives.outcome: Reject a condition that changes the intended population.
objectives.assessment: Identify an accidentally dropped valid record.
objectives.remediation: Compare the retained row IDs, not just the count.

lessons.title: Loops and reliable aggregations
lessons.motivation: An aggregate carries forward all prior contributions and needs an honest denominator.
lessons.progression: Start with three errors, then an empty batch and unequal paired lists.
lessons.terms: for, range, enumerate, zip, accumulator, count, loop invariant.
lessons.math: Finite sums, means and paired residuals.
lessons.worked: With errors=[-2,0,2], initialize total=0, then run the separate loop statement for error in errors: total += error*error. The final total is 8; mean square is 8/3. Resetting total inside the loop loses earlier terms.
lessons.misconception: The final loop value is not the aggregate; zip stops at the shorter input.

objectives.outcome: Trace a bounded loop and half-open range.
objectives.assessment: Predict visited indices and iteration count.
objectives.remediation: Expand range into an explicit index list.

objectives.outcome: Compute an aggregate without dropping or resetting contributions.
objectives.assessment: Repair a sum/count trace and explain its denominator.
objectives.remediation: Write one accumulator row per observation.

objectives.outcome: Maintain row pairing with enumerate/zip and detect unequal lengths.
objectives.assessment: Identify a silently truncated feature/target pair list.
objectives.remediation: Check input lengths and paired row IDs before iteration.

objectives.outcome: Explain a zero-count division guard and bounded iteration.
objectives.assessment: Choose the safe branch for an empty filtered batch.
objectives.remediation: Separate count validation from mean calculation.

lessons.title: Functions turn repeated steps into contracts
lessons.motivation: A function is a reusable input/output promise, not a printed screen message.
lessons.progression: Compose two calls, then change a default/mutation case.
lessons.terms: def, parameter, argument, return, local scope, default, side effect.
lessons.worked: Define predict(area, weight, bias) with body return area*weight+bias. A separate call predict(2,100,50) returns 250. Printing 250 without returning it leaves the call result None.
lessons.misconception: print is not return; a local assignment need not change the caller's name.

objectives.outcome: Identify parameters, arguments and local variables in a supplied function.
objectives.assessment: Label a changed prediction call and its local state.
objectives.remediation: Trace a call frame separately from caller variables.

objectives.outcome: Return a usable result instead of only printing it.
objectives.assessment: Repair a two-function pipeline whose first call returns None.
objectives.remediation: Follow the returned value into the next calculation.

objectives.outcome: Compose small validation and prediction functions in order.
objectives.assessment: Choose an ordered call sequence for a new record.
objectives.remediation: Draw the intermediate input/output types.

objectives.outcome: Recognize mutable-default and unexpected-input mutation risks.
objectives.assessment: Choose an explicit no-mutation/default-None repair from supplied options.
objectives.remediation: Compare successive calls and caller-owned data.

lessons.title: Comprehensions as readable transformations
lessons.motivation: Map and filter are different data operations; feature/target pairs must stay together.
lessons.progression: Translate a loop, then expose separately filtered row IDs and a duplicate key.
lessons.terms: list/dict comprehension, expression, filter predicate, key/value mapping.
lessons.worked: [value*2 for value in [1,2,3] if value>1] gives [4,6]; it does not produce a sum. A dictionary keyed by duplicate customer IDs overwrites earlier entries.
lessons.misconception: A filter can silently change the target population; a comprehension is not automatically a reduction.

objectives.outcome: Translate a one-level loop into a list comprehension without changing order.
objectives.assessment: Select an equivalent comprehension for a changed feature list.
objectives.remediation: Expand it into the original loop.

objectives.outcome: Preserve feature/target alignment when filtering records.
objectives.assessment: Repair separately filtered feature and target lists using one record-level predicate.
objectives.remediation: Compare retained row IDs on both sides.

objectives.outcome: Predict a dictionary comprehension with duplicate keys.
objectives.assessment: Choose final keys/values and identify overwritten data.
objectives.remediation: Trace each insertion into a keyed table.

objectives.outcome: Choose readable explicit code over an unsupported nested shortcut.
objectives.assessment: Identify a supplied equivalent simple loop/comprehension.
objectives.remediation: Separate map, filter and reduce stages.

lessons.title: Debugging, exceptions and imports
lessons.motivation: An error is information about a violated input contract; suppressing it can fabricate data.
lessons.progression: Follow a conversion traceback, then compare narrow handling with a plausible logic bug.
lessons.terms: traceback, SyntaxError, TypeError, ValueError, IndexError, try/except, raise, module, import.
lessons.math: Domain validation and error propagation; a failed calculation is not zero.
lessons.worked: float('unknown') raises ValueError. except ValueError: mark_invalid() is safer than silently returning 0; import math; math.sqrt(9) gives 3.
lessons.misconception: Catching every exception does not fix bad data; importing is not training or running an entire model.

objectives.outcome: Locate the failing line and classify a supplied exception.
objectives.assessment: Select error class and offending operation in a new trace.
objectives.remediation: Read the final traceback frame and input type.

objectives.outcome: Handle invalid input explicitly without fabricating a valid zero.
objectives.assessment: Choose a narrow exception branch and explain why the record is invalid.
objectives.remediation: Contrast error, missing and legitimate zero outcomes.

objectives.outcome: Explain an explicit import and distinguish module name from variable name.
objectives.assessment: Repair a preset math/module name lookup.
objectives.remediation: Follow import binding to the named function.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish a syntax error from a logic error with plausible output.
objectives.assessment: Select the minimal repair and a counterexample that exposes the logic bug.
objectives.remediation: Run the author-owned good/bad fixtures side by side.

lessons.title: Reproducible small programs and local data
lessons.motivation: Reliable programs validate data at an explicit resource/schema boundary; instances own separate state.
lessons.progression: Trace a bundled record through validation, then separately inspect two tiny instances.
lessons.terms: CSV, JSON, schema, context manager, StringIO, instance, attribute, method.
lessons.math: A valid table needs stable row/column meaning before modeling.
lessons.worked: A bundled CSV containing area='2', age='' needs numeric conversion and explicit missingness, not a guessed 0. A tiny Record class stores area per instance; changing one instance must not change another.
lessons.misconception: A successful parse does not validate schema or units; class attributes and instance state are not interchangeable.

objectives.outcome: Validate a bundled record's schema, conversion and missingness before use.
objectives.assessment: Reject a malformed new CSV/JSON record and explain its unsafe default.
objectives.remediation: Apply the supplied field/type/nullability checklist.

objectives.outcome: Explain context-managed reading and deterministic relative asset paths.
objectives.assessment: Order read/parse/validate/close steps without using an arbitrary path.
objectives.remediation: Trace resource lifetime in a with block.

objectives.outcome: Assemble a small import/function/validation processing flow.
objectives.assessment: Choose the full preset program that produces a validated feature list.
objectives.remediation: Return to P05 contracts and P07 explicit errors.

objectives.outcome: Recognize instance attributes and a simple method in a practical class (introductory).
objectives.assessment: Predict two independent Record instance values.
objectives.remediation: Compare per-instance dictionaries; no inheritance required.
